name: Gullet Prime
description: Gullet Prime is a massive gas giant that seems to consume everything in its vicinity, its immense gravity having cleared its orbital neighborhood of all but the most distant objects. The atmosphere is a deep, hungry red that darkens to near-black at the poles, where magnetic anomalies create coronal discharges visible from neighboring planets. A planet-spanning hurricane occupies the equatorial region, its rotation so powerful it creates visible atmospheric layering like the ridges of a throat.

The planet's gravitational influence is felt far beyond its atmosphere, creating a tidal effect that warps the orbits of nearby bodies over time. The dense atmosphere compresses sound waves into physical phenomena, and deep-atmospheric probes have recorded pressure pulses that propagate outward like the contractions of a living gullet. The research station in high orbit experiences temporal drift, with clocks running measurably slower than identical instruments at a safe distance.

The temporal distortion has no confirmed cause, though it strengthens proportionally with proximity to the planet. Atmospheric fauna of enormous scale have been observed in the mid-layers, their movements coordinated across the planetary surface in ways that suggest communication through pressure waves. The exotic matter detected in the deep atmosphere is denser here than at any other known gas giant, and its distribution follows the temporal distortion gradient exactly.

Gullet Prime's combination of exotic matter, temporal distortion, and atmospheric fauna makes it one of the most scientifically significant gas giants in known space. The research station is perpetually underfunded and understaffed, as the temporal effects make long postings psychologically difficult. Energy corporations and military research divisions both seek exclusive access to the exotic matter reserves, and the regulatory vacuum in this frontier region means control will likely go to whoever can maintain a presence longest.
